First, I’m a kid. Then there’s Type 1 Diabetes.

I’m Aviva. I’m a Youth Ambassador for Breakthrough T1D because I enjoy helping my community. I like to give back through food security initiatives at Ampowering, by walking runways to raise disability awareness, or helping elementary kids find their buses on Safety Patrol. I also live with Type 1 Diabetes. This means that my days come with extra data, glucose checks, alarms and balancing, but it has never been the whole story. This is my site for raising awareness and funds for T1D research.

About Aviva

A student, an advocate, and a kid first

My story starts with the things I love doing. Type 1 Diabetes is part of it, an important part, but it comes second.

Who I am

A student with a busy, active life, school, sports, runways, volunteering and speaking up for causes I care about. The photos on this site are my real life, not a stock picture of diabetes.

My T1D story

I was diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes a few days after my 7th birthday. My birthday party had to be cancelled as I was in the ICU. When I got back to school, I saw that I was suddenly not invited to sleepovers or parties. All the kids wanted to know what the “patch” on my arm was. I was confused and sad. I decided to start AvivaCares so no other child feels that way again. My diagnosis became the starting point for learning, speaking up, and helping other people understand what T1D really is and what it isn’t.

Why I speak up

I created Aviva Cares to demystify T1D, educate classmates and teachers, and raise funds for a cure through Breakthrough T1D, turning my own journey into action for others.

“When you live with Type 1 Diabetes, every single day is a science experiment… it just means living life with extra data and a lot of resilience.”

From “Welcome to Aviva Cares,” in Aviva’s Stories

My diaversary is a celebration

Every year, we mark my diaversary, the anniversary of my diagnosis, not as a sad date, but as a celebration: another year of doing hard things, learning my body, and living without limits. Resilience is worth celebrating.

T1D 101 for Schools & Friends

The two-minute version for teachers, coaches & classmates

Just the essentials, in plain language. Aviva explains both topics in full, in her own words, in Aviva’s Stories. This page is only the short version, and each card takes you to the full story on its own page.

The Short Version · CGM Alarms

What that beep means

Aviva wears a Continuous Glucose Monitor (CGM), and sometimes it beeps at school. It is not a phone or a game — it is an alert about her blood sugar, and a high and a low each need a different response.

Read Aviva’s full guide — Story No. 2 →

The Short Version · The Basics

Type 1 is not Type 2

Type 1 Diabetes is an autoimmune condition. It is not caused by eating sweets, and it is not the same as Type 2 Diabetes — the difference matters, because it changes the support a kid with T1D needs.

Read Aviva’s full explainer — Story No. 3 →

Breakthrough T1D Fundraiser

Help fund the research that changes lives

I’m Aviva, and I fundraise for Breakthrough T1D, the leading global organisation funding Type 1 Diabetes research. I do it because I live this every day, the checks, the alarms, the balancing, and because every gift helps drive progress toward better treatments, and ultimately cures, for every kid like me.

Every dayof checking, balancing and carrying on — that’s what your gift lightens
One teamAviva, her family, her school and her community, raising voices together
One goalbetter treatments today, and cures for Type 1 Diabetes

Automated insulin delivery

Smarter systems that use CGM data to adjust insulin automatically, easing the daily balancing act.

Cell therapies

Research working to restore the body’s own insulin-producing cells — a path toward life without constant management.

A cure, together

Fundraising turns stories like mine into momentum for the whole T1D community — people, not just dollars.

Personal Story & Mission Story No. 1

Welcome to Aviva Cares — Turning My T1D Journey Into Action

When you live with Type 1 Diabetes, every single day is a science experiment. You balance carbs, insulin, activity levels, stress, and sleep — all while trying to just be a kid, go to school, and hang out with friends. I created Aviva Cares to demystify T1D, educate classmates and teachers, and raise funds for a cure through Breakthrough T1D. T1D isn’t caused by eating too much sugar, and it doesn’t mean stopping sports or active hobbies; it just means living life with extra data and a lot of resilience. Welcome to our community!

School Advocacy & Peer Awareness Story No. 2

What That Beep Means — A Guide to CGM Alarms in the Classroom

If you hear a high-pitched tune or a repeated buzz from my desk or backpack, don’t worry — I’m not playing a game on my phone! That sound comes from my Continuous Glucose Monitor (CGM). It measures my blood sugar continuously and alerts me if my levels are going too high or dropping low.

  • High Alarms: Means my body needs extra water or an insulin adjustment.
  • Low Alarms: Means I need quick-acting sugar immediately (like juice boxes or fruit gummies).
  • How classmates can help: You don’t need to panic! Just let the teacher know if I look tired or shaky, and give me a minute to treat my low.

T1D Education Story No. 3

Type 1 vs. Type 2 Diabetes — Busting the Biggest Myths

One of the most common things people ask is: “Did you get diabetes from eating too many sweets?” The short answer is: No.

  1. Type 1 Diabetes (T1D): An autoimmune condition where the body’s immune system accidentally attacks the insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas. Nothing I ate or did caused it, and it cannot be cured by diet or exercise.
  2. Type 2 Diabetes: A metabolic condition where the body becomes resistant to insulin or doesn’t produce enough.

Understanding the difference helps eliminate stigma and ensures kids with T1D get the exact medical support and understanding they need at school and sports.
